findings.F1: Across all coins, a coin's 24-hour move is partly reversed over the next 24 hours, on the non-overlapping 24-hour grid: the slope of the next 24-hour unusual move (in usual moves) on the past 24-hour move is -0.0915 (t -11.74, 16238 cases). In the extreme quintiles, the falls (z -1.24) are followed by +0.468 % (t 4.40, 3251 cases) and the rises (z +1.32) by -0.322 % (t -3.27, 3249 cases).
findings.F2: The 24-hour reversal holds in every coin: the mean unusual move in the reversal direction on the extreme quintiles is +0.28 % to +0.59 % (t 1.54 to 3.50, about 1090 cases each). That is about 0.05 of a usual 24-hour move (5.5 % to 9.5 %) and about twice the 0.19 % cost of a trade. It is positive in 2018 to 2023 (+0.20 % to +0.68 %, t up to 3.93) and near zero in 2024 (-0.09 %, t -0.48) and 2025 (+0.04 %, t 0.17).
findings.F3: The reversal does not depend on the weekend or on thin volume. On Sunday day-ends, the slope of the next 48-hour unusual move on the past 48-hour move is -0.024 (t -0.77, 1951 cases), no steeper than on other weekdays (-0.028 to +0.035). The 24-hour extreme-quintile reversal is +0.31 % (t 2.65) in the lowest volume tercile, against +0.44 % (t 3.51) and +0.43 % (t 3.26) in the middle and highest terciles.
findings.F4: The 24-hour reversal is carried by the most volatile stretches. In the top quintile of past-week realised volatility, the correlation of the past 24-hour move with the next 24-hour unusual move is -0.18 (3422 cases). In the four lower quintiles it is +0.02 to -0.02.
findings.F5: The book loses before fees on every coin: mean gross trade return -0.38 % to -1.89 %, win rate 22 % to 32 %, 1796 trades in all. Its worst day is Sunday, with a mean daily return of -1.93 bps (t -6.53).
findings.F6: A separate hour-of-day pattern appears in all six coins. Returns are higher in the hours ending 21:00 and 22:00 UTC (+4.83 bps, t 5.98; +3.74 bps, t 4.85), lower in 02:00 to 03:00 UTC (-2.44 bps, t -3.19; -3.39 bps, t -4.65) and lower in 14:00 UTC (-4.18 bps, t -4.46). Each coin gains +3.7 to +4.8 bps an hour at 21 to 22 UTC (t 2.5 to 3.9), and 7 of 8 years are positive. Over the two hours that is about 0.085 %, below the 0.19 % cost of a trade.

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return is partly reversed over the next 24 hours: the larger its 24-hour rise against its usual 24-hour move, the larger its fall over the following 24 hours, and the larger its 24-hour fall, the larger its rebound, on any day of the week.
ideas.consequence: After a coin's unusually large one-day move, a trader takes the opposite side for the next day, and refuses to chase the move.
ideas.name: daily moves partly reverse

ideas.idea: A coin's 24-hour return is reversed over the next 24 hours more strongly the higher its realised volatility over the past 7 days: in its most volatile weeks, the larger the 24-hour move against its usual move, the larger the opposite move over the next 24 hours.
ideas.consequence: A trader fades a coin's large one-day moves mainly when the coin has been unusually volatile over the past week, and holds back in its calm weeks.
ideas.name: volatile-week daily reversal
